mild.summary: Minor cut or scrape. Any individual can provide care.

steps.title: Wash your hands
steps.instruction: Wash hands with soap and water for 20 seconds before touching the wound.

steps.title: Stop the bleeding
steps.instruction: Apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth or gauze for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Clean the wound
steps.instruction: Rinse the wound under cool running water. Avoid scrubbing.

steps.title: Apply antiseptic
steps.instruction: Dab a thin layer of antiseptic ointment around the wound.

steps.title: Cover the wound
steps.instruction: Place a sterile bandage over the wound. Change daily.

moderate.summary: Deeper cut with moderate bleeding. First aid is sufficient but monitor closely.

steps.title: Apply firm pressure
steps.instruction: Press a clean cloth firmly over the wound for at least 10 minutes without lifting.

steps.title: Elevate the wound
steps.instruction: Raise the injured area above heart level to slow bleeding.

steps.title: Do NOT remove embedded objects
steps.instruction: If something is stuck in the wound, leave it. Stabilize it with bandages.

steps.title: Bandage tightly
steps.instruction: Wrap firmly with sterile gauze. Check fingers/toes remain warm and pink.

steps.title: Seek medical attention
steps.instruction: Visit a clinic within a few hours for stitches if needed.

severe.summary: Heavy bleeding or deep wound. CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES IMMEDIATELY.

steps.title: CALL EMERGENCY NOW
steps.instruction: Dial 112 (or local emergency) immediately. Do not delay.

steps.title: Apply maximum pressure
steps.instruction: Press hard on the wound with any clean cloth. Do not release pressure.

steps.title: Keep patient still and warm
steps.instruction: Lay the patient flat. Cover with a blanket. Keep them talking if conscious.

steps.title: Monitor breathing
steps.instruction: Watch chest rise and fall. If breathing stops, prepare for CPR.

steps.title: Wait for help
steps.instruction: Stay with the patient. Do not give food or water.

burn_care.name: Burn Care
burn_care.description: Thermal burns from heat, fire, or hot liquids

mild.summary: First-degree burn (red, no blisters). Any individual can treat at home.

steps.title: Cool the burn
steps.instruction: Run cool (not cold) water over the burn for 10-20 minutes.

steps.title: Remove jewelry
steps.instruction: Gently remove rings, watches, or tight clothing near the burn before swelling starts.

steps.title: Apply aloe vera or moisturizer
steps.instruction: Use pure aloe vera gel or fragrance-free moisturizer. Avoid butter or oils.

steps.title: Cover loosely
steps.instruction: Use a sterile non-stick bandage. Do not wrap tightly.

moderate.summary: Second-degree burn with blisters. First aid first, then seek care.

steps.title: Cool the burn
steps.instruction: Run cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice.

steps.title: Do NOT pop blisters
steps.instruction: Leave blisters intact — they protect against infection.

steps.title: Cover with sterile gauze
steps.instruction: Apply a loose, sterile non-stick dressing.

steps.title: Take pain reliever
steps.instruction: Paracetamol or ibuprofen can help (check allergies first).

steps.title: Visit a clinic
steps.instruction: Burns larger than 3 inches need professional evaluation.

severe.summary: Third-degree burn or large area. CALL EMERGENCY IMMEDIATELY.

steps.title: CALL EMERGENCY NOW
steps.instruction: Dial 112 immediately. Severe burns are life-threatening.

steps.title: Do NOT remove stuck clothing
steps.instruction: If clothing is stuck to the burn, leave it. Removing it causes more damage.

steps.title: Cover with clean cloth
steps.instruction: Use a clean dry sheet. Do not apply water or ointment.

steps.title: Watch for shock
steps.instruction: Keep patient lying down with feet elevated. Cover to keep warm.

steps.title: Monitor breathing
steps.instruction: If smoke inhalation is suspected, prepare for airway issues.

severe.summary: ALWAYS SEVERE. Begin CPR immediately and call emergency.

steps.title: Check responsiveness
steps.instruction: Tap shoulders and shout. If no response, proceed.

steps.title: CALL EMERGENCY NOW
steps.instruction: Dial 112 or ask someone nearby to call. Put phone on speaker.

steps.title: Position the patient
steps.instruction: Lay flat on back on a firm surface. Tilt head back, lift chin.

steps.title: Start chest compressions
steps.instruction: Place hands center of chest. Push hard and fast: 100-120 per minute, 2 inches deep.

steps.title: Continue until help arrives
steps.instruction: Do not stop. If trained, give 2 rescue breaths every 30 compressions.
